descriptors.R: nominee of the party that has controlled Congress since 1861 and directed Reconstruction over the President's vetoes; the general who commanded the Union armies to victory, with no previous civil office
descriptors.D: nominee of the opposition party, which demands the immediate restoration of the Southern states, amnesty and state control of suffrage; a former wartime governor of a large Northern state

compile_desc.R: the party that has controlled Congress since 1861 and directed Reconstruction
compile_desc.D: the opposition party, which opposes congressional Reconstruction

others_line: Other candidates on very few ballots (answer "other").
never_name: Grant, Colfax, Seymour, Blair, Andrew Johnson, Lincoln, Chase, Pendleton or Stanton

slice_sources.men: 1860 and 1870 censuses interpolated to November 1868, white men 21+ outside the former Confederate states; in most Northern states Black men could not yet vote (the Fifteenth Amendment came in 1870); calibrated to certified returns.
slice_sources.women: No women could vote for president in 1868; women 21+ shown for population only.
slice_sources.south-white: 1860 and 1870 censuses interpolated to 1868, white adults in the former Confederate states; Mississippi, Texas and Virginia were not yet readmitted and cast no vote, and Florida's legislature chose its electors; some former Confederates were barred from voting by state law; calibrated to certified returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1860 and 1870 censuses interpolated to 1868, Black adults in the former Confederate states; Black men voted for the first time in a presidential election under the Reconstruction Acts and federal troops, but only in the seven former Confederate states that held a popular vote, and Klan violence cut their vote sharply in Georgia and Louisiana.
slice_sources.immigrants: 1860 and 1870 censuses interpolated to 1868, foreign-born white men not yet naturalized; many Midwestern, Western and some Southern states let declarant aliens vote, elsewhere only naturalized men could.
